issues.description: Class UniqueTable constructor parameter mismatch: In template_repository/dd.py the UniqueTable.__init__ is declared as def __init__(self, size: int) -> None and assigns self.size (lines 177-181), but the template immediately instantiates UT = UniqueTable() with no argument (line 278), which would raise a TypeError at import time. In the solution (solution_repository/dd.py) UniqueTable.__init__ is declared with no parameters (def __init__(self) -> None, lines 177-181) and the solution also instantiates UT = UniqueTable() (line 277). This inconsistency between the template's constructor signature and how it is instantiated (and the solution's no-arg constructor) will cause a runtime/import error and will block students from running or testing the provided template.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the template UniqueTable constructor signature match the solution and the template usage: change 'def __init__(self, size: int) -> None:' to 'def __init__(self) -> None:' and remove any use of self.size (or otherwise ensure any required size is provided where UT is instantiated). This preserves the intended API (no-arg constructor) and prevents import-time errors. Alternatively, if a fixed size is truly required, update the template instantiation to pass a concrete integer (e.g., UT = UniqueTable(1024)), but aligning to the solution (no-arg __init__) is recommended.
